final.executive_summary: Underweight AAPL and execute the trim at the next open: rebalance from 1.49% of the $99,596.07 account (4.797 shares at 309.90, average cost 314.85, unrealized -$23.74) to a 1.0% target weight (~3.21 shares, ~$996 notional), selling roughly 1.58 shares for about $0.49 in 10-bps fees. Keep that residual as a participation coupon into the binary Q4 FY26 print, not as a return engine, because the bear case is a gross-margin-duration and valuation argument, not a franchise or solvency break. Size is the only functioning risk control here — the 300.00 'stop' is narrative, not a working order — so no adds anywhere between 302 and 317, and no rebuild before the gross-margin guide is actually delivered. Horizon 1-3 months, re-underwritten at the late-October/early-November FQ4 print.
final.investment_thesis:
Direction is settled and not a close call: all three risk seats independently concluded that 1.49% of a 98.5%-cash account is not the right exposure into a binary gross-margin print, and none defended full size. The aggressive seat framed the exit, the conservative called the 300.00 stop what it is — 'a sentence in a memo' — citing the 7/31 -7.35% gap on 132.5M shares and the 6/25 -6.11% gap on 107M, and the neutral seat did the arithmetic both others avoided: from the current 4.797 shares, the full bear objective at 281.90 costs only ~$134, or 13.5 bps of equity. That is the real dispute, and it is why the answer is a trim expressed in valuation and margin-risk terms rather than a liquidation.

The bear wins the question that decides the near term: the duration of the 50.06% Q3 gross margin. COGS in the quarter ended 6/27 reflects inventory laid in before the 2026 memory-cost shock — raw materials and purchased parts +260% to $7.645B, total inventory +94% to $11.09B — so the record margin is the most mean-reversion-prone line in the dataset, and the forward-buy is equally a ~$7.6B commitment at elevated input prices flowing through COGS over the next two to four quarters. The only forward mix proxy supplied, deferred revenue amortization +4.3% against revenue +16%, undercuts the 'Services-led, durable margin' story, and the 357 bps of expansion cannot be decomposed at all — no segment, product or geographic tags exist in this dataset. Add the ETR step-up from 15.39% to 17.58% (~$0.18 of 9M EPS), net intangibles +91%, other non-current liabilities +$13.5B to $55.1B with no footnote, and buybacks decelerating 12% to $62.1B while FCF rose 52.5% — the opposite of the price-insensitive-bid signal the bull draws, and the ~$300-380 repurchase range is an FY26 average, an upper bound rather than a floor. Valuation seals it: ~34x FY26 EPS on the ~$9.05 derived estimate (~38x annualizing Q3's $2.02), with a ~2.8% clean FCF yield below the risk-free rate, and a $110.2B 9M FCF figure that is roughly $94-95B after stripping ~$15-16B of working-capital and other-liability timing.

The tape confirms de-risking rather than adding. At 309.90 AAPL sits below the 50 SMA (310.88), the 10 EMA (310.27) and the Bollinger middle (311.50) simultaneously, has closed under a flat 50 SMA three sessions running, carries an unrecovered -7.35% gap from 333.43, and was rejected at 320.28 on 8/20 on 40.96M shares with volume since decaying to 25.87M, the lightest of August. Both MACD lines remain below zero and the histogram's repair is decelerating (last four bars +0.058, +0.081, +0.145, +0.087), so repair is stalling short of the signal cross while ATR has compressed to 7.23 (2.33% of price) — the exit is cheap now and expensive after 300.00 breaks.

The bull wins the franchise question decisively, and that is why this is Underweight and not Sell. Balance-sheet transformation is real: net cash ~$62.2B versus $33.7B, D/E 0.78x, current ratio above 1.0 for the first time, $110.2B of 9M FCF even on the conservative working-capital adjustment, capex at 1.9% of revenue with no hyperscaler AI-capex exposure, and price still 9.93% above a rising 200 SMA at 281.90 with the 50 SMA above it. Nothing reported is broken — this is a margin-duration and multiple argument, so the correct expression is reduced exposure with a live residual, not zero.

Where I overrule the seats. I reject the conservative 0.5% (~1.61 shares): its churn argument does not differentiate, since both proposals are a single next-open trade, the $46.31 cumulative fee figure is an account-history number set against the $23.74 mark on one open position, and at $498 a 10% gap pays five basis points — a souvenir that is neither exit nor position. Its rebuild trigger, a close holding 310-311, is a ~0.4% move from spot: noise with a threshold painted on it. I equally reject the aggressive rebuild to 2.0-2.5% at 322-328: you cannot use 34x as the reason to sell and then pay ~36x for the same fragile margin three to four percent higher, and 320.28 has already been tagged and rejected once. The neutral construction wins: 1.0%, which caps the loss to the 300.00 invalidation at roughly three basis points of equity and to the 281.90 bear objective at roughly nine — a size that functions as its own stop — with any rebuild capped at 1.5% and gated on the delivered guide. I also note the neutral's fair correction on denominators: the multiple is a choice (28x rolling forward, 34x on the estimate, 38x annualized), which is precisely why that argument justifies trimming rather than exiting, and why the rebuild cap is 1.5% rather than 2.5%.

Conditions on the residual are narrative only, not working orders. Cut toward 0.5% or flat on a daily close below 300.00 — the 7/31 gap low, ~1.4 ATR below spot — on expanding volume, with 293.39 then 281.90 (the rising 200 SMA, a further ~9%) as the downside map; do not average down into either. Rebuild to a maximum of 1.5% only after the FQ4 gross-margin guide is delivered at 49.5% or better with revenue growth at or above 12%, and either two consecutive closes above 320.28 on >50M shares with MACD back above zero, or a defended 302-300 base with the histogram turning positive — accepting only the breakout path forces us to buy the most expensive version of being right. Also flagged: this account holds 98.5% cash earning nothing, which is the single largest implicit position in the book, but that is outside this instrument's remit and I am not authorizing it here. Stated gaps, not papered over: no segment/product/geographic revenue or margin split, so 50.06% durability is unattributable; no options chain or implied-vol data, so no protective put or collar can be priced for the October window; the sentiment report is unavailable in this run, so there is no crowd-momentum argument in either direction; the cause of the 7/31 gap and the composition of the $55.1B other non-current liabilities are unverifiable in this dataset; and the $9.05 FY26 EPS is a derived estimate, so the 300.00 price target is technical, not valuation-derived.
